name: Microsoft Entra ID

verdict.topBlocker: Customer tenants on Microsoft's default consent policy block end-user consent for mail, calendar, files and chat scopes, so a tenant admin must grant consent even after publisher verification.
verdict.summary: The only wait is Partner Center verification of your AI Cloud Partner Program account (usually 3-5 business days); after that, publisher verification takes minutes and lets users in other tenants consent without the risky-app step-up. Marketplace/AppSource, the Entra app gallery and Microsoft 365 App Compliance are optional; the real limit is that customer-tenant consent policies often require an admin to approve agent-style scopes such as Mail.Read.

steps.title: Create a multitenant App Registration from a work/school account
steps.detail: In the Microsoft Entra admin center (Identity > Applications > App registrations > New registration), choose 'Accounts in any organizational directory' (optionally plus personal Microsoft accounts) so that other companies' users can connect. Register it from a work or school (Entra) account, because apps registered with a personal Microsoft account can't be publisher verified.

steps.title: Configure Platform Redirect URIs
steps.detail: Add redirect URIs on the Authentication page for Web, Single-page, or Desktop/Mobile platforms. URIs must use HTTPS (except localhost) and match exact character casing.

steps.title: Generate client credentials (prefer a certificate)
steps.detail: Under Certificates & secrets, upload a certificate (recommended for production) or create a client secret. Secrets last at most 24 months and Microsoft recommends under 12, so plan rotation. Copy the secret value right away; it isn't shown again.

steps.title: Configure least-privilege delegated permissions
steps.detail: Add the Microsoft Graph delegated permissions under API permissions, plus openid, profile and offline_access. Note that Mail.*, Calendars.*, Files.Read.All, Sites.Read.All and Chat.* can't be user-consented in tenants on the Microsoft-managed default policy, so a tenant admin must consent. Avoid Directory.ReadWrite.All and application permissions unless they are truly needed.

steps.title: Execute OAuth 2.0 Auth Code & Token Requests
steps.detail: Test the login flow by constructing requests to the /authorize endpoint, receiving authorization codes, and exchanging them at the /token endpoint for access and refresh tokens.

steps.title: Test cross-tenant user consent and admin consent
steps.detail: Sign in from a second Entra tenant (not your home tenant) to see the real consent experience, including risk-based step-up. Test the admin consent URL https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/adminconsent?client_id={client-id} and the customer's admin consent workflow request path.

steps.title: Enroll in Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (partner global account)
steps.detail: Enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program in Partner Center as the partner global account (PGA), not a location account. Use a business email whose domain matches a DNS-verified custom domain on your Entra tenant, and associate the tenant with the PGA. Have business registration documents and domain registrar documents ready, and complete identity verification.

steps.title: Wait for Partner Center account verification (usually 3-5 business days)
steps.detail: Microsoft checks the email, identity, employment (domain documentation) and business registration. Watch Account settings > Legal info > Verification Summary and answer any document requests quickly. Only the primary contact receives the emails.

steps.title: Mark the app as publisher verified
steps.detail: Sign in with MFA as an Application Admin or Cloud Application Admin who is also a CPP Partner Admin or Account Admin. Set a non-onmicrosoft.com publisher domain, open Branding & properties, choose Add Partner ID to verify publisher, and enter the PGA Partner One ID. This takes minutes; then check the blue badge using prompt=consent.

requirements.note: A Microsoft Entra ID tenant and a work/school or personal Microsoft account are required to register applications in the Entra admin center.
Publisher domain must be configured on the app registration and must match the domain verified under the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account.
A verified Partner One ID from a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program partner global account is required for publisher verification.

scopes.note: Standard delegated permission to read the signed-in user's profile.
Delegated permission to read user mail; subject to user or admin consent depending on tenant policies.
Standard OIDC scope requested to obtain a refresh token for long-lived access.
Admin-restricted scope requiring Global Administrator consent in target organizational tenants.

blockers.symptom: User receives a warning screen that the app is unverified and risky, or is blocked from granting consent.
blockers.cause: The multitenant application is not Publisher Verified, and risk-based step-up consent policies in the user's tenant block consent.
blockers.unblock: Complete Publisher Verification by associating a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account with the app registration.

blockers.symptom: Error AADSTS50011: The reply URL specified in the request does not match the reply URLs configured for the application.
blockers.cause: The redirect URI sent in the authentication request does not match any redirect URI registered in the Entra admin center.
blockers.unblock: Ensure exact scheme, host, port, and path case matching when configuring redirect URIs in Authentication settings.

blockers.symptom: User is shown an error stating they are not authorized to consent to the requested permissions.
blockers.cause: The application requested high-privilege or admin-restricted permissions such as Directory.ReadWrite.All.
blockers.unblock: Request a Global Administrator in the target tenant to grant tenant-wide consent, or revise app scopes to non-admin delegated permissions.

claims.text: App registration is initiated by selecting New registration under App registrations in Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Browse to Identity > Applications > App registrations and select New registration .
claims.note: Confirmed against primary source in review 2026-11-01.

claims.text: Client secrets are created under Certificates & secrets in the app registration.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Select Certificates & secrets > Client secrets > New client secret .

claims.text: Client secret lifetime is limited to a maximum of 24 months.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Client secret lifetime is limited to two years (24 months) or less.
claims.note: Confirmed against primary source in review 2026-11-01.

claims.text: Redirect URIs are added on the Redirect URI configuration tab under Authentication.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: On the Redirect URI configuration tab, select Add Redirect URI .
claims.note: Confirmed against primary source in review 2026-11-01.

claims.text: New SPA redirect URIs are added by choosing the Single-page application platform on the Authentication page. The manifest editor is only one way to change an existing URI's type to spa.

claims.note: Corrected in review round 2, 2026-11-01; it previously said: SPA redirect URIs must be set to type spa using the application manifest editor.

claims.text: Admin-restricted permissions need tenant-wide admin consent. For delegated permissions this can come from a Cloud Application Administrator, Application Administrator, AI Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator. Microsoft Graph application permissions (app roles) need a Privileged Role Administrator. Global Administrator is not the only role that can grant it.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Cloud Application Administrator, AI Administrator, or Application Administrator, for granting consent for apps requesting any permission for any API, except Microsoft Graph app roles
claims.note: Corrected in review round 2, 2026-11-01; it previously said: Admin-restricted permissions require Global Administrator consent.

claims.text: The authorization code flow redirects the user to the Microsoft identity platform /authorize endpoint.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: In the flow, the app redirects the user to the Microsoft identity platform /authorize endpoint.

claims.text: The offline_access permission is a standard OIDC scope requested to obtain a refresh token.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: The offline_access permission is a standard OIDC scope that's requested so that the app can get a refresh token.
claims.note: Confirmed against primary source in review 2026-11-01.

claims.text: An access token is requested by sending a POST request containing the authorization code to the /token endpoint.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: The app uses the authorization code received in the previous step to request an access token by sending a POST request to the /token endpoint.
claims.note: Confirmed against primary source in review 2026-11-01.

claims.text: Delegated permissions allow the application to perform operations on behalf of the signed-in user.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Delegated permissions , also referred to as scopes : The permissions exposed by Microsoft Graph and that represent the operations that the app can perform on behalf of the signed-in user.

claims.text: Application permissions allow the app to access data on its own without a signed-in user.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Application permissions : Also called app roles , allow the app to access data on its own, without a signed-in user.

claims.text: Microsoft Marketplace (AppSource) SaaS offer: For publishers who want discovery or to sell through Microsoft. It is not needed for OAuth; Microsoft documents automated steps in minutes but gives no duration for the manual certification phase.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Offers submitted to Microsoft Marketplace must be certified before being published.

claims.text: Microsoft 365 App Compliance - Publisher Attestation: A self-service security questionnaire, renewed yearly, that produces a public docs page for enterprise security reviewers; useful when customer admins will be asked to grant mail or files consent.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Publisher Attestation is a self-service process where app developers (ISVs) complete a set of questions about their security practices

claims.text: Microsoft 365 Certification: A paid audit through Claranet (pentest if none in the last 12 months) for selling to security-strict enterprises; the ISV gets a 14-day window for initial documents and 60 days (+60 discretionary) for evidence, but no total review time is stated.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: ISV will work with audit firm to pay for the certification.

claims.text: Microsoft Entra App Gallery listing: Only for SaaS vendors who want SSO (SAML/OIDC) or SCIM provisioning to show up in customers' Enterprise apps gallery; needs a Partner One ID and isn't needed for Graph OAuth.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Is publisher verification the same as the Microsoft Entra application gallery? No.

claims.text: The Microsoft-managed default user consent policy (default for new tenants) excludes Mail.*, Calendars.*, Files.Read(Write).All, Sites.Read(Write).All, Chat.*, Contacts.*, Tasks.*, People.Read and others from end-user consent: An email, calendar or files agent cannot be self-connected by ordinary users in most tenants, so your onboarding must route customers to a tenant admin through the admin consent URL or the admin consent workflow.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: End users can consent for any user consentable delegated permissions EXCEPT

claims.text: Risk-based step-up consent (on by default) turns user consent into an admin requirement for unverified multitenant apps that ask for more than basic permissions: Without publisher verification even low-risk scopes beyond sign-in/profile fail with AADSTS90094 for users in other tenants, which makes publisher verification practically required.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: This step-up capability is enabled by default, but it results in a behavior change only when user consent is enabled.

claims.text: Tenants can disable user consent, or allow it only for verified publishers and low-impact permissions (microsoft-user-default-low): Some customers will never allow user consent, so the agent must support an admin-consent-first onboarding path.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Allow limited user consent only for apps from verified publishers and apps that are registered in your tenant

claims.text: Microsoft Graph application permissions (app roles) can only be granted by a Privileged Role Administrator; apps with assignment required always need admin consent: Background or daemon agent access to all mailboxes needs a highly privileged customer admin to approve it, which slows sales.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Privileged Role Administrator, for granting consent for apps requesting any permission, for any API.

claims.text: Refresh tokens last 90 days by default (24 hours for SPA redirect URIs) and can be revoked by password reset or admin action: A long-running agent must use a confidential (web) client, rotate refresh tokens, and handle invalid_grant by asking the user to reconnect.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: 24 hours for single-page applications... 90 days for all other scenarios.

claims.text: Outlook throttling: 10,000 requests per 10 minutes and 4 concurrent requests per app per mailbox; 130,000 requests per 10 seconds per app across all tenants; 429 with Retry-After: An agent that scans mail has to use delta queries or change notifications and honour Retry-After, not poll.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: 10,000 API requests in a 10-minute period | v1.0 and beta endpoints

claims.text: Client secrets expire after at most 24 months (12 months or less recommended): Plan secret rotation or use certificates, or every customer connection breaks when the secret expires.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: You can't specify a custom lifetime longer than 24 months.

reviewAdditions.text: The Microsoft-managed default consent policy (default for new tenants) blocks user consent for Mail, Calendars, Files/Sites .All, Chat, Contacts, Tasks and other permissions regardless of publisher verification, so admin consent is the normal path for email or calendar agents.
Risky consent requests show AADSTS90094 unless the customer has the admin consent workflow enabled.
Publisher domain can't be *.onmicrosoft.com; you need a DNS-verified custom domain on the tenant.
Publisher verification isn't supported in national clouds or Azure AD B2C tenants.
PKCE is recommended for all client types, including confidential web apps.
Refresh tokens: 90 days by default, 24 hours for spa redirect URIs; they replace themselves on use.
Outlook throttling limits per app per mailbox (10,000 requests per 10 min, 4 concurrent) and a global per-app limit of 130,000 requests per 10 s.
Partner Center verification usually takes 3-5 business days; only the primary contact gets the document requests.
